title: How Adam Robinson grew RB2B to $1M ARR with founder-led LinkedIn content
summary: Adam Robinson explains why founder-brand content on LinkedIn replaced outbound for RB2B. He covers the sales motion around it, how to write hooks, handling backlash, using paid thought-leadership ads, and why AI should not write your posts.

principles.text: People connect with people, so build a founder brand instead of a company page.
principles.quote: people are not on social media to connect with companies people are on social media to connect with people period even on LinkedIn right like period

principles.text: A person builds audience affinity at a fraction of the cost and time of a brand.
principles.quote: you can create the Affinity around a person that you could create around a brand in like one1 100th of the time with one1 100th of money because we're set up to feel that way

principles.text: The founder-brand motion: connect with ICP, post for 60 days, then ask for a demo.
principles.quote: in the beginning it's outbound connection campaign to your ICP you get them to accept you post great content you wait 60 days you ask for a demo it's 80% conversion rate because they think you're some sort of a celebrity

principles.text: Commit to posting until you find your voice; expect it to take about a year.
principles.quote: for me it took a year I put I'm I'm a very Focus foced and maniacal person in many ways I put a lot yeah I put a lot into this and it took me a year

principles.text: Build credibility in the hook with specifics, numbers and bold claims, and spend most idea time on hooks.
principles.quote: you have to treat LinkedIn as though this person who's reading it has never heard of you and you have to build however you can as much credibility as possible in the hook

principles.text: A polarizing view you truly believe is a gift; expect haters but never fake controversy.
principles.quote: if you have a polarizing view that you believe in that the world has not yet accepted that's one of the best gifts that's ever been given in social media
